territorySponsorship._note: Sponsorship is a proven, repeatable line, not a projection: Santam signed R9m over three years (R2.5m -> R3.0m -> R3.5m) to be attached to this product in South Africa, a ~150k-golfer market. territorySponsorship._sizing: New-territory deals are set below the SA run-rate at entry and grow with the installed base. They are NOT scaled linearly off golfer counts — sponsorship is negotiated and lumpy, and a linear scale off a 25M-golfer market would produce figures no sponsor would sign. Every figure here is a live input on the Sponsorship tab.

valuationModel.comps: No listed comparable exists for an insured skill-prize platform. The multiple is set against what can be evidenced, not borrowed from US consumer-subscription comps.
valuationModel._multiplePolicy: One flat revenue multiple at every forward milestone (2026-08-04). The previous shape — 4.77x implied at entry, 2.74x at 2029, 6x at 2032 — dipped then spiked, which reads as three numbers picked to hit a target rather than a method. A single multiple is what an investor expects, and it means the milestones move only with revenue. Entry stays at whatever the round implies (R53.3m post / R11.2m revenue = 4.8x), so the multiple COMPRESSES as the company scales — the direction a sceptic expects.
valuationModel.multipleBasis: 3.0x revenue, flat at every forward milestone. The round itself implies 4.46x on 2026 forecast revenue, so the multiple COMPRESSES as the company scales. No multiple expansion is assumed anywhere.
valuationModel._horizonNote: The R1bn horizon was removed 2026-08-05 on the founder's instruction. It extended a subscriber growth rate to total revenue, which implied simulator attach reaching ~11.7% of all Korean rounds. Do not reinstate without a modelled basis.

insuranceModel._source: GetLucky_Insurance_Model.xlsx — the Santam underwriting submission. Reproduced independently 2026-08-05; every figure below ties to it.
insuranceModel._why: This is the reason the structure changed. A subscription that buys unlimited insured swings has premium fixed and exposure unbounded — at 16 par-3 attempts a month against a $10 subscription the cover runs at a loss ratio above 100%. Charging per entry collects the premium on the same swing that creates the risk, which is what makes it underwritable.
insuranceModel._breakeven: Aces would have to occur 2.51x more often than amateur odds predict before the cover stops making money.

engagement._note: Reduced from 4 rounds a month. 24 rounds a year is a keen amateur; 48 was not defensible.

insuranceModel.status: Underwriting submission prepared for Santam via Indwe. No revised policy is bound on these terms as at August 2026.

blendedStructure._why: Investors want recurring revenue; an insurer cannot cover unlimited swings for a fixed premium. The resolution is a CAPPED allowance, not unlimited: exposure per member per month becomes a known number, so it can be priced.
blendedStructure.tradeUpLadder: Pay on the tee to move that swing up: $5 for $2,500, $10 for $10,000, $50 for $50,000, $100 for $100,000.
blendedStructure._neutral: The blend is neutral to the insurer: 31.9%, identical to pay-per-play alone, because the included swings are priced at the same target loss ratio.
blendedStructure.unlimitedCounterfactual: 16 attempts a month at the $10,000 tier is $12.80 of expected claim against $2.40 of premium — a 533% loss ratio. That is why unlimited cannot be written.
